One OAuth client in your own Google Cloud project lets each person connect their own Google account: Gmail, Calendar, Search Console and Analytics, read only, whichever the apps you run ask for. The same page covers Sign in with Google, which is a separate client.

**Used by:** [OpenSEO](/docs/apps/openseo) for Search Console and Google Analytics (the `identity`, `search-console.read` and `analytics.read` sets); [OpenCRM](/docs/apps/crm) for Gmail and Google Calendar (the `gmail.read` and `calendar.read` sets).

**Ways to connect:** connect accounts, sign in.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Google account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)
- **Settings:** `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Built in:** nothing to add, only the client to set

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/google-workspace/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `pnpm everyapp provider show google-workspace` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

1. Signed in to Google, [create a Cloud project](https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate) (for example `EveryApp`). With Google Workspace, put it in your organization.
2. Enable the APIs behind the sets your apps use (the table below): for OpenSEO, the [Search Console API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/searchconsole.googleapis.com), the [Analytics Admin API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/analyticsadmin.googleapis.com) and the [Analytics Data API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/analyticsdata.googleapis.com); for OpenCRM, the Gmail API and the Google Calendar API.
3. Set up the [consent screen](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview): an app name people will see, a support email, and the audience: **Internal** (your Workspace only, no review) or **External**.
4. On [Data Access](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/scopes), add the scopes of those sets and no others: `webmasters.readonly` and `analytics.readonly` for OpenSEO, `gmail.readonly` and `calendar.readonly` for OpenCRM.
5. [Create a client](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients): type **Web application**, and under **Authorized redirect URIs** add the redirect URI above. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client secret**, or select **Download JSON**.
6. **External** only: while the app is in Testing, add each person under **Audience → Test users**. Their access lasts 7 days at a time until you publish the app and Google verifies it.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLIENT_ID GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Google account (who you are) | `openid`, `email`, `profile` |
| `gmail.read` | Gmail (read-only) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly` |
| `calendar.read` | Google Calendar (read-only) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly` |
| `search-console.read` | Search Console (read-only) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly` |
| `analytics.read` | Google Analytics (read-only) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  "google-workspace": { access: "read", scopes: ["gmail.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show google-workspace` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Google**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `pnpm everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.

## Search Console

For an app that lists the `search-console.read` set, OpenSEO among them:

1. Enable the [Google Search Console API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/searchconsole.googleapis.com) in the client's project.
2. Add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly` on the consent screen's [Data Access](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/scopes) page.
3. Each person connects their own Google account, one that can see the site in Search Console.

## Google Analytics

For an app that lists the `analytics.read` set, OpenSEO among them:

1. Enable the [Google Analytics Admin API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/analyticsadmin.googleapis.com) and the [Google Analytics Data API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/analyticsdata.googleapis.com) in the client's project.
2. Add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly` on the consent screen's [Data Access](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/scopes) page.
3. Each person connects a Google account with access to the GA4 property.

## Sign in with Google

`Continue with Google` on your Gateway's sign-in page, for people you've invited. It's another way into the same account. [Sign-in](/docs/sign-in)

### Make the OAuth app

1. Open [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials) and create an OAuth client ID (Web application).
2. Add the redirect URL `https://<your gateway>/api/auth/callback/google`. It asks only for `openid`, `email`, `profile`: who someone is, nothing an app could act with.
3. Copy what the Gateway needs:
   - `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID`: The OAuth client's Client ID (ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com)
   - `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET`: The OAuth client's Client secret.

- An OAuth consent screen still in Testing only signs in the test users listed on it; publish it for everyone else.

### Turn it on

```bash
pnpm everyapp signin add google
```

It asks for each value, the secret at a hidden prompt, and the button is on the sign-in page as soon as it's done.

### Check it worked

`pnpm everyapp signin show google` shows each setting as set and the redirect URL. Then sign out and select the button.
